claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi feedstock can be prepared as a blend of elemental powders for in-situ alloying during LPBF.
An elemental powder blend can undergo controlled in-situ mixing and form the desired AlCrFeNiSi alloy during melt-pool processing.
Lower laser power or shorter laser pulses reduce the thermal load during LPBF.
Optimized laser pulse shaping is an example of a low-thermal-load LPBF regime suitable for in-situ alloying of AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed processing regime will produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The proposed processing regime will refine the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The resulting microstructure will have a more uniform phase distribution.
The resulting microstructure will have lower residual-stress concentrations.
In-situ alloying during melt-pool formation leads to more uniform elemental distribution.
Rapid solidification during in-situ alloying refines the microstructure.
A refined and compositionally uniform microstructure mitigates thermal-stress accumulation.
A refined and compositionally uniform microstructure enhances mechanical performance.
Compared with high-thermal-load processing of pre-alloyed powder, the proposed route will significantly reduce residual thermal stress.
Compared with high-thermal-load processing of pre-alloyed powder, the proposed route will increase tensile strength.
Compared with high-thermal-load processing of pre-alloyed powder, the proposed route will increase ductility.
The proposed route will simplify post-processing requirements.
The expected benefits are limited to miniature components processed within a controlled low-thermal-load window.
Efficacy for larger parts or substantially higher thermal inputs is unverified.
Residual stress, tensile behavior, ductility, grain size, and phase homogeneity will be compared between the proposed process and a conventional-process control.
Failure to obtain statistically significant stress reduction and mechanical-property improvement, or failure to obtain meaningful microstructural refinement, will falsify the hypothesis.
